media.caption: Select a MIDI track and double-tap FX1 to open CONTROL 1 SETUP. PB and AT show STK here; click encoder A or B to switch that position into CC mode.
media.alt: MIDI CTRL 1 SETUP showing PB and AT as STK, with CC1 7, CC2 1, CC3 2 and CC4 10.
media.credit: Cooper Scobey — local ot_emu framebuffer capture

media.caption: Click A and B in SETUP to switch both positions into CC mode. Each starts at CC0; this example leaves A at CC0 and turns B to CC127, then confirms with YES. Use controller numbers supported by your receiving instrument.
media.alt: MIDI CTRL 1 SETUP with CC0 in the first position and CC127 in the second position.
media.credit: Cooper Scobey — local ot_emu framebuffer capture

otUi.setup: Headless ot_emu; MKII panel; stopped transport; 128×64 LCD at integer scale 6.

media.caption: Press FX1 to return to CONTROL 1 and enable A or B with FUNC + encoder press. The headers identify CC0 and CC127; their enabled values are 64 and 32 here. Turn the encoder to send a value on the MIDI track’s output channel.
media.alt: MIDI CONTROL 1 on MIDI channel 01 showing CC0 at 64 and CC127 at 32, with the other four CC positions OFF.
media.credit: Cooper Scobey — local ot_emu framebuffer capture

otUi.setup: Headless ot_emu; MKII panel; stopped transport; 128×64 LCD at integer scale 6.

media.caption: Press FX2 to view CONTROL 2. Its headers show the assigned CC numbers, here 71–76, instead of slot names. All six values are OFF in this capture; enable a value before sending it.
media.alt: MIDI CONTROL 2 with controller numbers 71, 72, 73, 74, 75 and 76; all six values are OFF.
media.credit: Cooper Scobey — local ot_emu framebuffer capture

media.caption: Double-tap FX1 and click A again to restore native pitch bend. PB returns to STK while B keeps CC127, so the modes remain independent. Switching A back to CC later starts at CC0.
media.alt: MIDI CTRL 1 SETUP showing PB as STK in the first position while the second position remains CC127.
media.credit: Cooper Scobey — local ot_emu framebuffer capture
